stem: Which blood group is known as the 'universal donor'?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: Blood group O (particularly O−) is the universal donor for red blood cells because it lacks A and B antigens on the cell surface, so it won't trigger agglutination in recipients. AB+ is the universal recipient (accepts all groups).

stem: The Rh factor in blood is named after which organism?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: The Rh (Rhesus) antigen was first identified in Rhesus monkeys by Landsteiner and Wiener (1940). Rh+ means the antigen is present; Rh− means it is absent. Rh incompatibility can cause haemolytic disease in newborns.

stem: Which blood group is the 'universal recipient' for red blood cell transfusions?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: AB+ has both A and B antigens and the Rh factor — its immune system won't reject A, B, AB or O blood. Hence AB+ is the universal recipient for red cells. However, for plasma donations the rule reverses (AB is the universal plasma donor).

stem: ABO blood grouping is based on the presence of antigens on which cells?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: A and B antigens (glycoproteins) are located on the surface of red blood cells. The ABO system was discovered by Karl Landsteiner in 1901, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1930.

stem: A person with blood group A has which antibodies in their plasma?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: Blood group A has antigen A on RBCs and anti-B antibodies in plasma. Group B = antigen B, anti-A antibodies. Group AB = antigens A and B, no ABO antibodies. Group O = no A/B antigens, both anti-A and anti-B antibodies. The antibody is always against the antigen you DON'T have.

stem: Erythroblastosis fetalis (haemolytic disease of the newborn) occurs when:

options.option_text: Mother is Rh+ and baby is Rh−
Mother is Rh− and baby is Rh+
The baby has AB blood group

subject: Science — Biology
explanation: Rh− mother sensitised by Rh+ fetal blood develops anti-Rh antibodies. In subsequent Rh+ pregnancies, these antibodies cross the placenta and attack fetal RBCs. Prevented with Rh immunoglobulin (RhoGAM) injection after first delivery.

stem: Which of the following blood groups can donate plasma to ALL patients?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: AB plasma contains NO anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it won't attack any recipient's red cells — making AB the universal plasma donor. Note: this is the REVERSE of the red cell rule (where O− is universal donor). A key exam twist.

subject: Science — Biology
explanation: Vitamin K is essential for synthesising clotting factors II (prothrombin), VII, IX and X. Deficiency leads to excessive bleeding. Newborns receive Vitamin K injections at birth as their gut microbiome hasn't yet developed to produce it.

stem: The average lifespan of a red blood cell is approximately:
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: RBCs survive ~120 days before being removed by the spleen and liver. WBCs survive days to years depending on type. Platelets survive ~7–10 days. The 120-day lifespan is the basis for the HbA1c test (3-month blood sugar average).

stem: Which blood cells are primarily responsible for fighting bacterial infections?
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: Neutrophils (most abundant WBC at ~60–70%) are the first responders to bacterial infection — they engulf and destroy bacteria by phagocytosis. Lymphocytes handle viral immunity and antibody production. Thrombocytes (platelets) = clotting.

stem: The protein that carries oxygen in red blood cells is:
subject: Science — Biology
explanation: Haemoglobin (Hb) binds oxygen in the lungs (oxyhaemoglobin) and releases it in tissues. Each Hb molecule carries 4 oxygen molecules. Myoglobin stores oxygen in muscles; Albumin maintains blood osmotic pressure; Fibrinogen is a clotting factor.
